top_story: A sharp escalation in Yemen now carries the greatest regional weight: Houthi missile and drone strikes on 7 August killed at least 58 Saudi-backed government troops and also hit inside Saudi Arabia, reviving a front that had been relatively quieter and prompting Riyadh to warn of further attacks. In Lebanon, Israel’s 5 August strike in the south, which killed one and wounded 11 despite the June ceasefire, was followed by intensifying public anger over renewed strikes and displacement orders, then by rights groups’ 6 August assessment that the killing of journalist Amal Khalil may constitute a war crime. Together these developments show ceasefire frameworks fraying at both ends of the Arabian Peninsula and the Levant, with civilians, local media, and already fragile communities absorbing the immediate cost. The broader picture is a region where unresolved wars are slipping back into open escalation faster than political channels can contain them.
